79529.subject: How to Use Jev AI: The Complete Guide to TypeSafe's System One Model 🤖
79529.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/how-to-use-jev-ai

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
One of the researchers who helped build ChatGPT has just launched a model that cannot write a single word, and it may matter more to people who build software than any model release this year. Diogo Almeida, formerly of OpenAI, brought Jev out of stealth a week ago through TypeSafe AI. Jev does not generate text the way ChatGPT or Claude do. It makes decisions. Give it a predefined set of options, and it returns the choice plus a calibrated confidence. Think of it as a very smart switch statement: a 2016-style classifier with 2026-level intelligence.
Most AI products are built around models that write. They generate an answer, produce code, summarize a document, or reason through a problem one token at a time. Jev is built for a different and far more frequent job: deciding what software should do next.
Unsurprisingly, nobody got excited about that description. They got excited when builders started wiring Jev into real systems and posting the numbers, and the numbers were remarkable. Within a week of launch, Jev was on Vercel’s AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and Cloudflare Workers AI, and community catalogs listed hundreds of public builds. Three of them show the pattern just perfectly.
Matthew Berman used Jev to break down 724 live ads from 37 brands by hook, format, offer, call to action, awareness stage, and landing-page mismatch. He reported that the analysis took 40 seconds and cost just 9 cents in tokens. Of course, Jev accepts text, not images, and the post does not say how the ads were preprocessed. Yet, it still shows how a creative library becomes a searchable decision dataset instead of a folder of assets.
Another developer named Vechen inserted Jev into an active Codex run so it could raise GPT-6 Astra’s [ https://substack.com/redirect/52eea817-1028-4f57-a1bf-f7cf6be2f115?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] reasoning effort when the agent looked stuck and lower it during routine steps. He reported 50% lower Astra costs in his tests, faster runs, and preserved prompt caching. He reported the figure himself, and nobody has benchmarked it independently, but the architecture matters more than the number here. Instead of choosing a model once at the start, Jev controlled how much reasoning the system used at each stage of the task.
Jarrod Watts connected Jev to a MON-USDC price feed and built a trading bot with it. Given the price feed of an asset pair, Jev decides whether to buy or sell, and the bot executes real trades on Kuru’s on-chain order book on Monad, once every 300-millisecond block. The code is open source, and it proves a model decision can run inside a loop that fast.

Щоб і надалі користуватися цими службами iCloud, потрібно оновити план до iCloud+: https://setup.icloud.com/email/prefs/storage?path=STORAGE_AND_BACKUP/CHANGE_STORAGE_PLAN або звільнити місце в сховищі.


Оновіть план до iCloud+ з 2 ТБ за 9,99 € на міс.: https://setup.icloud.com/email/prefs/storage?path=STORAGE_AND_BACKUP/CHANGE_STORAGE_PLAN
